items.title: Section: One Hundred and Ten Kinds of Suffering Open — From the Single Suffering of Endless Wandering Through the Sting of Two Arrows to the Three Classical Sufferings of Pain, Conditioning, and Reversal

items.zh: 此中菩薩，於有情界觀見一百一十種苦，於諸有情修悲無量。何等名為百一十苦？謂有一苦。依無差別流轉之苦，一切有情無不皆墮流轉苦故。復有二苦。一、欲為根本苦。謂可愛事若變、若壞所生之苦。二、癡異熟生苦。謂若猛利體受所觸，即於自體執我我所，愚癡迷悶，生極怨嗟。由是因緣，受二箭受，謂身箭受及心箭受。復有三苦。一、苦苦，二、行苦，三、壞苦。
items.en: Among these, bodhisattvas observe one hundred and ten kinds of suffering throughout the realm of sentient beings, and on this basis cultivate the immeasurable of compassion towards them. What are these one hundred and ten kinds of suffering? There is one suffering: the suffering of undifferentiated wandering through birth and death, since there is not a single being who does not fall into this wandering suffering. There are, further, two sufferings. First, the suffering having desire as its root: the suffering produced when something cherished changes or is destroyed. Second, the suffering of delusion arising at the moment of ripening: when touched by an intensely painful bodily sensation, one grasps at a self and what belongs to that self within one's own being, becomes confused and distressed through delusion, and gives rise to intense resentment and lament — through this very cause and condition, one is struck by two arrows, the arrow of bodily sensation and the arrow of mental sensation. There are, further, three sufferings: first, the suffering of intrinsic pain; second, the suffering of conditioning; third, the suffering of reversal.

items.title: Section: Four Through Seven — Separation's Five Aspects, the Five Meditative Hindrances, Six Sufferings of Livelihood, and the Seven Classical Sufferings Each Unfolded Into Five

items.zh: 復有四苦。一、別離苦，謂愛別離所生之苦。二、斷壞苦，謂由棄捨眾同分死所生之苦。三、相續苦，謂從此後，數數死生，展轉相續所生之苦。四、畢竟苦，謂定無有般涅槃法諸有情類五取蘊苦。復有五苦。一、貪欲纏緣苦，二、瞋恚纏緣苦，三、惛沈睡眠纏緣苦，四、掉舉惡作纏緣苦，五、疑纏緣苦。復有六苦。一、因苦，習惡趣因故。二、果苦，生諸惡趣故。三、求財位苦。四、勤守護苦。五、無厭足苦。六、變壞苦。如是六種總說為苦。復有七苦。一、生苦，二、老苦，三、病苦，四、死苦，五、怨憎會苦，六、愛別離苦，七、雖復希求而不得苦。
items.en: There are, further, four sufferings: first, the suffering of separation, meaning the suffering produced by separation from what is loved; second, the suffering of severing, meaning the suffering produced by death's own abandonment of one's present bodily existence; third, the suffering of continuation, meaning the suffering produced by dying and being born again and again, one link after another, from this point onward; fourth, the ultimate suffering, meaning the suffering of the five grasped aggregates belonging to those beings who definitely possess no capacity whatsoever for complete nirvāṇa. There are, further, five sufferings: first, the suffering bound up with the entanglement of craving; second, the suffering bound up with the entanglement of hostility; third, the suffering bound up with the entanglement of dullness and drowsiness; fourth, the suffering bound up with the entanglement of restlessness and remorse; fifth, the suffering bound up with the entanglement of doubt. There are, further, six sufferings: first, the suffering of cause, meaning the cultivation of the causes of the lower realms; second, the suffering of fruit, meaning birth in the lower realms themselves; third, the suffering of seeking wealth and position; fourth, the suffering of diligently guarding it; fifth, the suffering of never feeling satisfied; sixth, the suffering of its eventual decay. There are, further, seven sufferings: first, the suffering of birth; second, the suffering of old age; third, the suffering of sickness; fourth, the suffering of death; fifth, the suffering of meeting what is hated; sixth, the suffering of separation from what is loved; seventh, the suffering of seeking yet not obtaining.

items.title: Section: Eight Through Ten Close the First Fifty-Five — Cold, Heat, Self-Inflicted Austerity, Nine Kinds of Loss, and Ten Material Lacks From Food to Companionship

items.zh: 復有八苦。一、寒苦，二、熱苦，三、飢苦，四、渴苦，五、不自在苦，六、自逼惱苦，謂無繫等諸外道類。七、他逼惱苦，謂遭遇他手塊等觸、蚊虻等觸。八、一類威儀多時住苦。復有九苦。一、自衰損苦，二、他衰損苦，三、親屬衰損苦，四、財位衰損苦，五、無病衰損苦，六、戒衰損苦，七、見衰損苦，八、現法苦，九、後法苦。復有十苦。一、諸食資具匱乏苦，二、諸飲資具匱乏苦，三、騎乘資具匱乏苦，四、衣服資具匱乏苦，五、莊嚴資具匱乏苦，六、器物資具匱乏苦，七、香鬘塗飾資具匱乏苦，八、歌舞伎樂資具匱乏苦，九、照明資具匱乏苦，十、男女給侍資具匱乏苦。
items.en: There are, further, eight sufferings: first, the suffering of cold; second, the suffering of heat; third, the suffering of hunger; fourth, the suffering of thirst; fifth, the suffering of lacking self-mastery; sixth, the suffering of self-inflicted distress, referring to those non-Buddhist ascetics who go about unclothed and the like; seventh, the suffering inflicted by others, referring to encountering the touch of another's hand or a thrown stone, or the touch of mosquitoes and gadflies; eighth, the suffering of remaining too long in any single posture. There are, further, nine sufferings: first, the suffering of one's own decline; second, the suffering of another's decline; third, the suffering of a relative's decline; fourth, the suffering of the decline of wealth and position; fifth, the suffering of the decline of health; sixth, the suffering of the decline of discipline; seventh, the suffering of the decline of correct view; eighth, suffering in this present life; ninth, suffering in lives yet to come. There are, further, ten sufferings: first, the suffering of lacking the requisite of food; second, the suffering of lacking the requisite of drink; third, the suffering of lacking the requisite of transport; fourth, the suffering of lacking the requisite of clothing; fifth, the suffering of lacking the requisite of ornament; sixth, the suffering of lacking the requisite of household implements; seventh, the suffering of lacking the requisite of fragrance and adornment; eighth, the suffering of lacking the requisite of song, dance, and music; ninth, the suffering of lacking the requisite of illumination; tenth, the suffering of lacking the requisite of male and female attendants.

items.title: Section: The Second Fifty-Five Opens — All-Encompassing Suffering, Vast Suffering, and Suffering Belonging to Every Realm of Rebirth

items.zh: 當知復有餘九種苦。一、一切苦，二、廣大苦，三、一切門苦，四、邪行苦，五、流轉苦，六、不隨欲苦，七、違害苦，八、隨逐苦，九、一切種苦。一切苦中，復有二苦。一、宿因所生苦，二、現緣所生苦。廣大苦中，復有四苦。一、長時苦，二、猛利苦，三、雜類苦，四、無間苦。一切門苦中，亦有四苦。一、那落迦苦，二、傍生苦，三、鬼世界苦，四、善趣所攝苦。
items.en: One should understand that there remain nine further kinds of suffering: first, all-encompassing suffering; second, vast suffering; third, suffering belonging to every realm; fourth, suffering from wrong practice; fifth, wandering suffering; sixth, the suffering of wishes unfulfilled; seventh, the suffering of injury; eighth, suffering that relentlessly follows; ninth, suffering of every kind. Within all-encompassing suffering, there are, further, two kinds: first, suffering produced by past karmic cause; second, suffering produced by present circumstance. Within vast suffering, there are, further, four kinds: first, prolonged suffering; second, intensely severe suffering; third, suffering of overwhelming, mixed variety; fourth, uninterrupted suffering. Within suffering belonging to every realm, there are also four kinds: first, the suffering of hell-beings; second, the suffering of animals; third, the suffering of the ghost realm; fourth, the suffering belonging to the favourable realms.

items.title: Section: Wrong Practice's Five Forms — Provoking Retaliation, Mismanaging Food, and the Self-Inflicted Austerity of Believing Present Pain Erases Past Karma; Then Wandering's Six Uncertainties

items.zh: 邪行苦中，復有五苦。一、於現法中犯觸於他，他不饒益所發起苦。二、受用種種不平等食，界不平等所發起苦。三、即由現法苦所逼切，自然造作所發起苦。四、由多安住非理作意，所受煩惱、隨煩惱纏所起諸苦。五、由多發起諸身語意種種惡行，所受當來諸惡趣苦。流轉苦中，復有六種輪轉生死不定生苦。一、自身不定，二、父母不定，三、妻子不定，四、奴婢、僕使不定，五、朋友、宰官、親屬不定，六、財位不定。自身不定者，謂先為王、後為僕隷。父母等不定者，謂先為父母乃至親屬，後時輪轉，反作怨害及惡知識。財位不定者，謂先大富貴，後極貧賤。
items.en: Within suffering from wrong practice, there are, further, five kinds: first, the suffering arising, in this present life, from having mistreated another, who then repays that mistreatment in kind; second, the suffering arising from consuming food that unbalances the body, thereby unbalancing its own elements; third, the suffering arising when, driven by present pain, one deliberately inflicts further suffering on oneself; fourth, the suffering that arises from afflictions and their secondary afflictions, entangling one who habitually dwells in improper attention; fifth, the suffering of future lower rebirth, resulting from habitually engaging in every kind of bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct. Within wandering suffering, there are, further, six kinds of suffering produced by the uncertainty of wandering through birth and death: first, uncertainty of one's own status; second, uncertainty of one's parents; third, uncertainty of one's spouse and children; fourth, uncertainty of one's servants and attendants; fifth, uncertainty of one's friends, officials, and relatives; sixth, uncertainty of one's wealth and position. Uncertainty of one's own status means having once been a master, later becoming another's servant. Uncertainty of parents and the rest means having once been parents or other relatives to one another, only to later, through the turning of rebirth, become instead a source of enmity and harm, even a source of bad influence. Uncertainty of wealth and position means having once been greatly wealthy and honoured, later becoming utterly poor and lowly.

blocks.text: The bodhisattva cultivates compassion by contemplating the suffering of beings, catalogued in remarkable detail: one hundred and ten kinds. The list is meant to be read slowly, as a meditation.

"There is one suffering: undifferentiated wandering, since not a single being does not fall into it." Two: suffering born of desire, and suffering rooted in desire (Venerable Miào Jìng: affliction-desire desires; object-desire is desired). And "two arrows": the sage cannot escape the bodily arrow, but escapes the mental one (Venerable Miào Jìng). Three: the suffering of pain, of change, and of conditioned existence.

Separation; severing; continuity; and "ultimate suffering: the aggregates of beings who have no capacity for final nirvāṇa". The five hindrances; six sufferings of livelihood; seven classical sufferings, each unfolded.

Cold, heat, hunger, thirst, lack of freedom; self-inflicted austerity (Venerable Miào Jìng: ascetics scorching themselves with fires on four sides and the sun above, believing suffering ends suffering); harm by others. Nine kinds of loss; ten kinds of lack, from food to companions.

All-encompassing suffering (from past causes and present conditions), vast suffering, suffering in every realm, and suffering from **wrong practice**: provoking retaliation; mismanaging food; and "believing present pain erases past karma" (Master Cháng Bǎi: the view of some outsiders).

quiz.q: In the hundred and ten sufferings, what is the "one suffering"?
options: undifferentiated wandering, into which every being falls
quiz.why: "There is one suffering: the suffering of undifferentiated wandering, since there is not a single being who does not fall into it." Master Cháng Bǎi: this is the greatest suffering, generally called the suffering of wandering.

quiz.q: "Struck by two arrows — the bodily arrow and the mental arrow." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: ordinary people only the body arrow
the body arrow is the five sense consciousnesses; sages still have it, but not the mind arrow
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the "bodily arrow" refers to the first five consciousnesses; the sage cannot yet escape the bodily arrow, but the mental arrow is gone.

quiz.q: In "suffering rooted in desire," how do the lectures distinguish object-desire and affliction-desire?
options: Miào Jìng: affliction-desire is the desiring, object-desire the desired; Cháng Bǎi: object-desire always implies affliction-desire, not vice versa
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: affliction-desire is the one that desires, object-desire what is desired. Master Cháng Bǎi: where there is object-desire there is always affliction-desire, but not the reverse — renunciants leave object-desire behind yet may still have affliction-desire.

quiz.q: Among the four sufferings, what is "ultimate suffering"?
options: the suffering of the grasped aggregates of beings with no capacity for nirvāṇa
quiz.why: "Fourth, ultimate suffering: the suffering of the five grasped aggregates of beings who definitely have no capacity for complete nirvāṇa." Master Cháng Bǎi: beings without seeds of the three vehicles' noble path. Venerable Miào Jìng: those who cannot trust the dharma or train in the noble path suffer permanently.

quiz.q: "Self-inflicted distress — non-Buddhist ascetics such as the Nirgranthas." How do the lectures assess it?
options: Miào Jìng: scorching themselves with five fires, thinking suffering ends suffering — a wrong view; Cháng Bǎi: the Nirgranthas believe enduring pain ends pain
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: these ascetics scorch themselves with fires on four sides and the sun above; believing suffering ends suffering is a wrong view. Master Cháng Bǎi: the Nirgrantha ascetics hold that enduring pain can end pain.

quiz.q: In the further nine, "all-encompassing suffering" divides into which two?
options: suffering from past causes, suffering from present conditions
quiz.why: "Within all-encompassing suffering there are two: suffering born of past causes and suffering born of present conditions." Master Cháng Bǎi: the former is the suffering of delusion at ripening mentioned earlier. Venerable Miào Jìng: divided by time, past and present.

quiz.q: The third wrong-practice suffering — "driven by present pain, deliberately causing more." What do the lectures say?
options: Cháng Bǎi: like the past-action fatalists, who think all present pain is from past deeds; Miào Jìng: pain sought out isn't past karma — it's endured for nothing
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: like outsiders who hold that all present suffering is caused by past evil deeds. Venerable Miào Jìng: suffering you take on deliberately is not past karma, so it is endured in vain — to end suffering you must cut afflictions.
